items.prompt: Return the length of the longest subsequence of s that reads the same forwards and backwards.
items.why: One string, palindrome, subsequence (skipping allowed), optimise → interval DP on s[i..j] with the 'drop an end' max.

items.prompt: Given a string, decide whether it is a palindrome, ignoring case and non-alphanumeric characters.
items.why: A yes/no check of the whole string, nothing to optimise → compare the ends and move inward. O(n), no table.

items.prompt: What is the minimum number of characters you must delete from s so that the rest is a palindrome?
items.why: What you keep must be a palindromic subsequence, so deletions = n − LPS. Interval DP over s[i..j].

items.prompt: Return the minimum number of single-character edits (insert, delete, replace) that turn word1 into word2.
items.why: Two different strings compared to each other → 2-D DP over a prefix pair (i in word1, j in word2), not one interval of one string.

items.prompt: Split s into pieces that are all palindromes, using as few cuts as possible. Return the number of cuts.
items.why: A minimum, not a list → precompute which s[i..j] are palindromes (interval DP), then a 1-D DP over prefixes. Backtracking would be exponential.

items.prompt: Return every possible way to split s into substrings that are all palindromes.
items.why: 'Return every' → the output itself is exponential, so you must enumerate choices of the next piece and undo them. A DP table can only prune.

items.prompt: Count how many substrings of s are palindromes (substrings at different positions count separately).
items.why: Palindromic substrings are decided by their ends and their inside → boolean interval table (or expand around centres). A window can't keep 'is a palindrome' up to date as it slides.

items.prompt: Find the length of the longest substring of s with no repeating characters.
items.why: Contiguous, single string, and the condition (no repeats) can be maintained incrementally → dynamic sliding window. Nothing about palindromes or two strings.
